_meta.purpose: What differs BETWEEN poster/packet series. One entry per series; SERIES=<id> selects it.
why: The country posters shipped rendering the UPG-100 packet's framing: the 'UNENGAGED PEOPLE
GROUPS' kicker, 'This packet is 1 of {n} UPG-100 lists', the UPG-100 narrowing funnel, and a
below-map block telling the reader to divide the set among thirty disciples. Coherent for ~30
There was no series parameter anywhere: packet.mjs and packet-render.js knew only one series,
so 'the packet' and 'the UPG-100 packet' were the same thing and nothing could disagree.
ONE mechanism for BOTH surfaces: packet.mjs AND generate.mjs read this
file, because the leak was in two independent places -- the packet strings and the poster's
own furniture (generate.mjs NETWORKS), which is not a packet string at all. Fixing only the
first would have left 'Thirty disciples' printing on every country poster.
_meta.default: upg100 -- absent or unknown SERIES resolves to upg100, so existing runs are unchanged.

keys.label: human name, for logs and error messages
keys.dataDir: repo-relative folder holding clusters.json and the selector/normalize/legend modules
keys.funnel: false DROPS the narrowing-funnel page entirely (it is a UPG-100 argument)
keys.strings: overrides merged OVER packet-strings.json's <locale> block, per key
keys.networks: the three below-map blocks generate.mjs prints; ENGLISH ONLY -- see note
keys.poster: the page-1 poster HEADER wording; ENGLISH ONLY, same reason as networks
keys.countryMode: true selects the COUNTRIES zone source (one sheet per country)

poster_keys.kicker: the small line above the title (generate.mjs:2426)
poster_keys.titleQualifier: the coloured words before the region name, e.g. 'Unengaged of' (:2427)
poster_keys.seriesName: the name in quotes on the Series line and in the side box (:1877, :1907, :2115)
poster_keys.sideBoxBody: that explainer's first paragraph (:2115); in the head-columns band **...** prints a bold run
poster_keys.strategyBody: the Jesus column's text: one paragraph, or a list of them; absent = poster-render's STRATEGY_DEFAULT
poster_keys.sideBoxMore: the explainer's further paragraphs: one, or a list; [] prints none; absent = poster-render's WHAT_IS_MORE

one_switch: SERIES is the ONE switch (2026-09-28). SERIES=country implies the country zone
source, the country series name and the country header strings. COUNTRIES=1 is kept as an
ALIAS that sets SERIES=country, so runs that predate this file keep working AND now get the
matching packet. Two parameters for one concept is what let a country render take the new
packet path while its header stayed UPG-100.
english_only_note: `networks` is English-only ON PURPOSE, not an oversight. generate.mjs performs no localization
at all: measured zero occurrences of PACKET_LANG, packet-strings or i18n in the file, and its
1,728 non-ASCII characters are entirely typographic (box-drawing, em-dashes, middots) with no
CJK, Arabic, Cyrillic or Devanagari -- so no translated string has ever been in it
(verified independently, 2026-09-28). The poster surface is English end to
end; `strings` below is the half that carries 11 locales.
translation_status: The `country` English below is a DRAFT, provisional, pending a product decision -- see
_draft_pending_decision on that entry. NO translations are to be made from it: a
paraphrase multiplied by 11 locales is 11 wrong strings. Once the English is approved, the
strings go to a HUMAN translator, which is this file's established practice --
all 11 locales of packet-strings.json carry real translations, never English echoes.

upg100.label: UPG100 — unengaged people groups, ~30 zoned lists

poster.sideBoxBody: This map is one of a {approxLists}-map set called the {seriesName} — a large, overwhelming target in the thousands, organised into clear groupings and displayed on maps and prayer lists. Each map comes with a prayer list of its fifty to a hundred people groups — their names, a representative photo, and more detail — to mobilise **informed intercession.**
poster.strategyBody: 2000 People Groups? Jesus’ disciples were faced with a similar problem, “How can we feed so many with only five loaves and two fish?” Through radical faith and miracle-expectant prayer, He focused on the few in front of Him — dividing the crowd and entrusting faithful men and women to serve the most strategic groups of fifties and hundreds (Mark 6:40).

networks: Each follower of Jesus takes their own map and prayer list, and sets apart a place to pray — some have hung a people-group map over their bed.
Each church dedicates a wall in one of its places of prayer, and keeps copies of the prayer list available for distribution.
Find leaders on the ground in these areas and give them the map and prayer list, to raise awareness of their unengaged neighbours.

country.label: Country — one poster per country, ~170 of them

poster.sideBoxHeading: What is a Country Prayer Map?
poster.sideBoxBody: This map is one of a {approxLists}-map set called the {seriesName} — one sheet for each country, naming the unreached people groups who live there so a reader can pray for them by name.

_poster_why: THE FOURTH LEAK SITE, found by reading the rendered page rather than a checker's verdict:
a SERIES=country poster still printed 'UNENGAGED PEOPLE GROUPS', 'Unengaged of West Africa',
'Series: List of 100 UPG's · map 11 of 28' and a side box calling it 'one of a 30-map set
called the List of 100 UPG's'. check:series-isolation passed because its vocabulary was a
HAND LIST of the phrases already found -- a PASS from it was only ever a lower bound.
seriesName 'Country Maps' is the series' agreed name, recorded in a generate.mjs comment
dated 2026-08-01, which also made the series name a parameterized field. The kicker says UNREACHED rather
than UNENGAGED because a country sheet lists the unreached groups living there, which is a
wider set than the unengaged -- see _draft_pending_decision; this wording is part of that draft.
_funnel_why: The funnel narrows every people group on earth down to THIS UPG-100 list (Project 2000/7000/
4700/700). That argument does not describe a country poster, and a page of true numbers about
the wrong thing is worse than no page. Dropped for country, 2026-09-28.
Dropping it also removes 12 of the 17 series-specific keys from the translation bill: a page
that does not render needs no locales.
_draft_pending_decision: THE ENGLISH BELOW IS A DRAFT, NOT APPROVED: provisional, pending a product decision on how
the three blocks should print. Do not translate, print at scale, or quote as final
until that lands; replace this key with the approved text when it does.

strings.map_page_sub: A prayer list of {count} unreached people groups who live here
strings.points_intro: One hour with God, five minutes each. Pray these twelve for the peoples of this country.
strings.christian_lede: This is the same grid — one human life in weeks. Now each box is a share of the people in this country. The shaded boxes are the evangelical share of their population; the rest are waiting.

_strings_why: FOUR keys, not seventeen. Judged by what each string SAYS rather than by matching UPG-100
vocabulary: 12 of the 17 are funnel_* keys and drop with the page above; `points` -- the 12
prayer points -- is INVARIANT, because those points are about a PEOPLE and a country poster is
still praying for the peoples within it; only its framing sentence (points_intro) names the
packet. christian_lede is ADAPTED, not replaced: the % Christian vs lost page is just as
meaningful for a country, so only 'the people in this list' is reworded.
Everything not listed here -- pray_blessed / pray_know / pray_do, the rhythms, the wheel, the
list header -- is series-invariant and inherited unchanged.
networks: Ask a disciple which country God has put on their heart, then give them that country's poster to print and prepare.
List the churches you know and ask each the same question, so every church has a poster to pray over together.
Ask which leaders you know who live in one of these countries, and give them their own country's map to pray for it specifically.
_networks_why: NOT a find-and-replace of thirty with a hundred and seventy. 'Divide the set among thirty
disciples' is coherent at 30 and incoherent at ~170 (172 countries + China + India, per
emit-countries.mjs), so the SHAPE was replaced: not 'split the set' but 'ask which one,
then give them that poster'. The numbers are gone from the headings for the same reason.

indiaState.label: India states and union territories — one poster for each of the 34 with people groups listed

poster.sideBoxHeading: What is a State Prayer Map?
poster.sideBoxBody: This map is one of a {approxLists}-map set called the {seriesName} — one sheet for each state and union territory of India, naming the unreached people groups who live there so a reader can pray for them by name.

_poster_why: A state poster is a country poster one level down: the Country Posters wall prints one for each of India's
states and union territories that has people groups listed (34 of 36; data/people-groups/india-states.json).
The country series' text cannot be reused: it would call Gujarāt's poster one of the ~170 'Country Maps',
one sheet for each country. The term is 'state and union territory', never 'province'. This is the default
wording and stays editable; a change is a strings-only follow-up.

strings.map_page_sub: A prayer list of {count} unreached people groups who live here
strings.points_intro: One hour with God, five minutes each. Pray these twelve for the peoples of this state.
strings.christian_lede: This is the same grid — one human life in weeks. Now each box is a share of the people in this state. The shaded boxes are the evangelical share of their population; the rest are waiting.

_strings_why: The country series' four keys with 'country' read as 'state'. Used by the Node generator; the browser
packet reads the localized packet-strings.json, which is series-invariant.
networks: Ask a disciple which state God has put on their heart, then give them that state's poster to print and prepare.
List the churches you know and ask each the same question, so every church has a poster to pray over together.
Ask which leaders you know who live in one of these states, and give them their own state's map to pray for it specifically.
